findings.english_quote: passages of the writings that plainly give an account of him
findings.issue: The draft neutralizes the accusatory force. καταλέγω with the personal genitive αὐτοῦ here means speaking against or accusing him, not merely recounting information about him. Simon's argument concerns passages that incriminate the Creator; the lexical note does not adequately represent this construction.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace this phrase with “passages of the writings that plainly accuse him” or “passages of the writings that plainly speak against him,” and revise the lexical note accordingly. The replacement requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: καὶ τοσοῦτον προαίρεσιν πόθον ἔχοντα διισχυρίζεσθαι
findings.english_quote: and to insist that he has so strong a desire for free choice
findings.issue: The note discusses the meaning of προαίρεσιν but omits a material attachment ambiguity: ἔχοντα can be understood as referring to Peter, represented earlier by σε, rather than to the Creator. On that reading, the phrase describes Peter's own purpose or eagerness in pressing his argument. The Creator-subject reading is defensible as an accusative-and-infinitive construction, but it must not be presented without this alternative.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note preserving the Peter-subject alternative and explaining why the main text instead takes ἔχοντα with the Creator. Specify the proposed accusative-of-respect treatment of προαίρεσιν rather than silently treating it as a genitive dependent on πόθον. Preserve the supplied Greek without emendation.

findings.source_quote: ἢ δι’ αὐτοῦ [τοῦ] θεοῦ ἢ ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ ἢ καὶ ἐξ οὐκ ὄντων [συμ]βέβηκεν, τῶν πρὸς τὶ ἐστὶν ἢ αἰεὶ ἦν
findings.english_quote: he came to be either through God himself or from himself, or even arose from things that do not exist; he belongs to the class of things that are relative to something, or he always existed.
findings.issue: The main text defensibly carries the evil one forward as the subject, but the disclosure is incomplete. The source note mentions possible influence from ὕλη on γέγονεν and συμβέβηκεν without clearly preserving the alternative that the following predications, including ἐστίν and αἰεὶ ἦν, concern the matter. It also asserts that the contextual choice is defensible without explaining why that grouping was selected.
findings.suggested_revision: Expand the source-quoted note to state explicitly that an alternative grouping concerns the origin and status of the matter from which the evil one arose, including whether that matter belongs among relative or dependent things or always existed. Explain the main text's decision to carry forward the evil one as subject from ὅθεν γέγονεν and the surrounding inquiry into his origin. This is an interpretive disclosure issue, not evidence of defective or unverified print.
